expected: Copyable workflow examples use actual registered names/keys and direct implementers to submit independent review before closure.

title: Coordination skills prescribe obsolete per-agent worktrees instead of the current development profile

excerpt.text:
> **Host gate (f00052):** `agent_worktree` is a host-scoped *capability*,
> off by default. Read `delendai.config.json#agentWorktree` (or the
> `--agent-worktree` CLI flag). If `false`/unset — do not call
> `proposals_agent_worktree`; commit to the active branch instead. This
> section documents the *primitive*; the *when-to-use* decision lives in the
> proposal playbooks and respects this flag.

First, read `delendai.config.json#agentWorktree` (or the `--agent-worktree`
CLI flag). If `false`/unset — do not call `proposals_agent_worktree`; commit
to the active branch instead. The `agent_worktree` path below applies only
when the host has enabled the capability.

- `none`: default for CI, audits, and any shared worktree. The plan does
  **not** include a worktree step — nothing is being pushed.
- `commit`: local single-agent work after a focused diff review. When
  `agentWorktree: true`, `delegate` already created the worktree; the
  plan still surfaces an explicit `agent_worktree create` step as a
  safety net for solo runs.
- `commit-and-push`: only inside a disposable `agent_worktree` (requires the
  host gate enabled). The plan prepends the `agent_worktree create` step
  and the persist step pushes to `origin agent/<branch>` — the branch
  the worktree owns.

- **Agents own work, not branches — git enforces it.** How work starts
  and lands (unit of work, pull request, merge or direct commit) is the
  project's `development` profile, and the server states it: in its
  connect-time instructions, `agent_bootstrap`, `overview` (`workModel`)
  and every refusal. Follow that, never this file or a design doc. The
  shared checkout never moves; `delendai work status` says where it
  stands.
- **No orphaned branches or stashes — always reconcile (this repo).**
  A unit ends in `delendai work publish` or `delendai work retire`
  (keeps its tip). Before closing a session run `bun run reclaim:orphans`:
  live units are no orphans; idle/abandoned ones print their remedy;

expected: Skills defer isolation, work-start and publication to the development profile/workModel and explain legacy per-agent behavior conditionally.
actual: Three skills choose between shared checkout and agent/* worktree using agentWorktree alone; they tell an unset/false host to commit on its active branch, or direct create/agent branch pushes when true. Current production registration has a separate unitWorktrees policy and refuses create under it because work enter owns the unit; bootstrap says the project profile is authoritative and a unit ends with publish/retire.
rootCause: Operational skills retained the earlier boolean capability model after isolation became project development policy.
impact: Following skill text can produce repeated deliberate refusal or attempt to work/ship outside the unit model; this directly frustrates canonical collaboration even when runtime gates hold.
recommendation: Resolve overview.workModel first and describe each current profile; route unit work through enter/publish/retire and retain agent_worktree instructions only for its applicable profile.

verification.method: own full skill read and source branch comparison
verification.confidence: high; no worktree or Git mutation

relationship: New instructional drift; distinct from work-ref retention/GC bugs already indexed.
multi-agent-coordination:244–246 additionally suggests force-transition closure; current canonical workflow should teach peer review, not use that as ordinary closure.
limits: Does not assert all hosts enable unit worktrees or that agent_worktree is universally invalid. Old behavior can remain valid under the per-agent profile; runtime refusal is counterevidence to silent creation.

title: Rules architecture skill says barrel-only extension wires a language, but the factory has an explicit adapter list

excerpt.text:
### Adding a new language — the OCP hinge

1. Create `src/lib/frameworks/languages/<lang>/<lang>.adapter.ts`
   that exports an `ILanguageAdapter` (priority + detection +
   optional `commands`).
2. Create `src/lib/frameworks/languages/<lang>/<lang>-command.provider.ts`
   if the linter has a non-ESLint shape.
3. Create `src/lib/frameworks/presets/data/<family>.ts` with the
   preset DATA (file contents as text).
4. Create `src/lib/frameworks/dogmas/<lang>.dogma.ts` with the
   `IDogmaAdapter` (ownership/error/null/naming/async/visibility/
   immutability/testing + bullets).
5. Add the new symbols to the three barrels
   (`languages/index.ts`, `presets/data/index.ts`,
   `dogmas/index.ts`).

**No other file changes.** The detectors, registries, manifest
writer, and tools stay untouched. This is the OCP hinge: the
plugin is open for extension (a 5-file PR) and closed for
modification (zero existing files change).

5. **Registry Entry** (`plugins/rules/src/lib/frameworks/registry/factory.ts`):

expected: A contributor recipe includes the actual composition-root registration needed for a new adapter to participate in default detection.
actual: The SOLID skill promises five files and no other modifications, says to export languages/index.ts, and forbids other modifications in its recipe. That barrel does not exist at snapshot. Factory selects a literal overrides.adapters ?? [...] list of sixteen adapter values; adding arbitrary adapter exports does not append to it. Core plugin-authoring correctly instructs adding the registry factory entry, so skills disagree.
rootCause: Desired automatic-extension architecture was documented as the shipped composition contract.
impact: A contributor can author/export a new adapter following the recipe yet never register it for default workspace detection, then spend time debugging an inert feature.
recommendation: Document current explicit factory wiring or implement/test actual adapter discovery; keep both authoring skills consistent and remove nonexistent barrel instructions.

title: Release skill still describes ten packages and release-on-main while current automation is opt-in

excerpt.text:
5. CI path: a push to `main` runs `derive-version.ts` (no flags) to decide
   `release`/`version`/`bump` from commits since the last `vX.Y.Z` tag — it
   never touches `package.json`; the git tag is the only source of truth for
   "what was the last released version".

## `publishOrder` (10 packages, fixed order)

From `tools/scripts/release/release-plan.ts` `PUBLISH_ORDER` — core first
(every plugin declares it as a `peerDependency`), then plugins:

```
packages/core
plugins/proposals
plugins/rules
plugins/memory
plugins/git
plugins/quality
plugins/search
plugins/notification
plugins/docs
plugins/deps
```

on:
    # DELIBERATE: a push to `main` no longer publishes.
    #
    # This used to be `push: branches: [main]` — "auto-release on every
    # push to main, el usuario no hace nada". That made merging the
    # promotion pull request the same act as publishing 61 packages to
    # the public npm registry, and the two are not the same decision:
    # `main` carrying the code is a statement about this repository,
    # publishing is a statement to everybody else. With no `vX.Y.Z` tag
    # in existence yet, the first such merge would have been the
    # project's first public release, derived automatically, at 0.1.1.
    #
    # Releasing is now something somebody asks for, in one of two ways:
    #   - push a `vX.Y.Z` tag, which is also what `derive-version` reads
    #     as the anchor for the NEXT version; or
    #   - run this workflow by hand from the Actions tab.
    #
    # Nothing else changed: the same derivation, the same PUBLISH_ORDER,
    # the same validate-build-publish-tag chain.
    push:
        tags: ['v*']

expected: Release instructions derive publish membership/order and release trigger from current source automation instead of frozen early inventories.
actual: Skill states a push to main runs release derivation and that fixed publish order is ten packages/core first. Current workflow explicitly says push to main no longer publishes; triggers are v* tags and workflow_dispatch. PUBLISH_ORDER begins contracts/state/sqlite/context-compiler before core and includes CLI/client/all published plugins. Operator preset table also freezes older membership.
rootCause: Release and operator skill tables retained early snapshots instead of linking to current derived inventories.
impact: Operators form the wrong expectation about whether landing code releases it and which dependency packages/order a deliberate release affects.
recommendation: Render or link to source-derived publish order and preset membership, and describe deliberate tag/manual release trigger with ownership/consent intact.

verification.method: own static comparison with exact workflow trigger block and release-plan data

relationship: New skill-level drift; existing publisher/provenance findings concern other behavior.
Do not revive the refuted prerelease candidate; no claim that prerelease rejection is a defect.
limits: No GitHub workflow/network state was inspected and no registry publication attempted; source workflow behavior is the scope.
